clauses.title: Scope
clauses.text: 1. Scope — Requirements of precast concrete lintels and sills.

clauses.title: Reinforced concrete lintels
clauses.text: 2.1.1 Reinforced concrete lintels — May be precast in one piece or in two pieces as a split lintel Note — The latter is lighter in mass, easier to handle and the air space between the pieces affords  insulation which is desirable especially if furring is not provided.

clauses.title: Lintel
clauses.text: 2.1.2 Lintel-cum-sun shade — For use over door, window and ventilator openings of exterior walls in buildings may also be precast.

clauses.title: U-shaped lintels
clauses.text: 2.1.3 U-shaped lintels — U-Shaped lintels are precast by stringing together U-shaped concrete masonry units as forms, and then placing reinforcement and pouring concrete to fill the forms.

clauses.title: Lintel bearing
clauses.text: 2.1.4 Lintel bearing — Reinforced concrete lintels for doors and windows shall be bonded into the masonry on either side of the opening. It is advisable to provide a bearing length approximately equal to the depth of the lintel.

clauses.title: Throatings
clauses.text: 2.1.5 Throatings — A 16mm wide throatings shall be provided to the soffit to external lintels.

clauses.title: Inserts for lintels
clauses.text: 2.1.6 Inserts for lintels — Provision shall be made for fixing screws to windows, door frames, curtain and blind fittings, etc, by means of timber or pre-formed inserts incorporated in the lintels during course of manufacture or by the forming of holes for inserts. For details refer to Figs. 1 to 4 of the standard.

clauses.title: General
clauses.text: 2.2.1 General —  General types of sills in common use-the slip sill and the lug sill. Both types are sloped on the top face to drain water away quickly. If projections are provided, they should project at least 40mm beyond wall face and be provided with a groove along the  lower outer edge to provide a drip. Lengths up to 1m may be cast in one piece.

clauses.title: Slip sills
clauses.text: 2.2.1.1 Slip sills — Slip sills are inserted after the wall proper has been built and therefore require no protection during construction.

clauses.title: Lug sills
clauses.text: 2.2.1.2 Lug sills — Lug sills are those with the ends projecting into the masonry wall. There are no vertical joints at the juncture of the sills and the jambs which is one of the advantages of the lug sill over the slip sill.

clauses.title: Dowell holes for sills
clauses.text: 2.2.2 Dowell holes for sills — Concrete sills to take metal windows shall be provided with holes 20mm diameter and 32 mm deep at prescribed distances from each end.

clauses.title: Projection of sills
clauses.text: 2.2.3 Projection of sills — The projection of sills, when provided, shall be not less than 40mm from the finished wall face.

clauses.title: Tolerances
clauses.text: 2.3Tolerances — For lintels, a tolerance of mm shall be allowed on cross-sectional dimensions and ± 6 mm on the length. In case of sills, a tolerance of mm shall be allowed on the cross-sectional dimensions and ± 3 mm on the length. For details refer to Figs. 5 to 7 of the standard.

clauses.title: Ultimate breaking load obtained
clauses.text: 3.1Ultimate breaking load obtained as prescribed in 7.1.1 of the standard shall not be less than the ultimate load which the lintel is  designed to carry. SUMMARY OF IS  9893 : 1981 PRECAST CONCRETE BLOCKS FOR LINTELS AND SILLS Note 1 — For details of material, refer to 3 of the standard. Note 2— For details of manufacture, or aspects such as construction, finish, mould, reinforcement, occuring etc, refer to 5 of the standard. For detailed information, refer to IS 9893:1981 Specification for precast concrete lintels and sills. +12 - 0 +0 - 6
